Executable comparison · runs offline in this page

One payment rule, two ways to authorize it

An app key may move XLM out of a smart account with transfer, only to the shop, and at most 10 XLM in any 100 ledgers. This page installs that rule twice: on an OpenZeppelin smart account, as a policy built by OZ Policy Builder, and on a Perch account, as a grant. It then sends both accounts the same requests and shows, at each step, what was signed, which contract checked what and in what order, and why the request was allowed or refused.

Not started. Starting compiles a 3.5 MB WebAssembly module in a worker in this tab.

Both accounts run as their real contract WebAssembly inside soroban-sim, a Soroban host compiled to WebAssembly, on a local ledger in a worker in this tab: no wallet, no RPC, no network request. Signatures come from throwaway Ed25519 keys. Verdicts, error codes, call traces, hashes and balances on this page come from that run; the explanations beside them cite the source lines (hover a grey tag for the full path). Without JavaScript the page shows the recorded reference run instead.

The task is a transfer from the smart account, amount capped, recipient pinned: one context, one rule, one signer. Perch grant documents bound amounts only through a windowed cap, so the shared task uses the window, which the OZ side gets from OpenZeppelin's spending_limit.

Who checks a payment

The allowed payment of step 2, as the host ran it. Solid boxes are contract calls that appear in the run's call trace. Dashed boxes are checks that make no contract call: the host checking a classic account's signature, and Perch's evaluator, which is a library linked into the account. Their place in the order comes from the cited source.

OZ authenticate, then run policies

callXLM.transfer(account, shop, 6 XLM)
asks from to authorize: from.require_auth() host stellar_asset_contract/contract.rs:206-215
hostentry 1 (the account's)
tree matches the call, not expired, nonce unused and consumed, signature payload hashed host auth.rs:2586-2600 host auth.rs:2631-2663; then the host calls __check_auth host account_contract.rs:150-172
callaccount.__check_auth
OpenZeppelin do_check_auth OZ storage.rs:629-689
in accountselect and check rules
one rule id per context (#3014); rule 1 exists, is unexpired and its scope is the XLM contract (#3000, #3002) OZ storage.rs:312-367; every payload signer is on a selected rule (#3016) OZ storage.rs:667-674
hostentry 2 (the app's)
app.require_auth_for_args((AuthDigestPreimage,)) OZ storage.rs:396-413; the host checks the app's Ed25519 signature against its G account's signers and consumes entry 2's nonce host account_contract.rs:175-263
callspending_limit.enforce
evicts spends at ledgers ≤ L − 100; refuses if the window total plus the amount exceeds 10 XLM (#3221); records the spend OZ spending_limit.rs:233-319
callpolicy-interpreter.enforce
the rule's signer set is the one installed (#204); then the stored predicate decides (#100 and other deny codes) OPB policy-interpreter/lib.rs:192-277

State for this rule lives in three contracts: the rule (scope, signers, policy list) in the account, the predicate and signer-set hash in the interpreter, and the spending window in spending_limit, the last two keyed by (account, rule id). The policies run in the order of their contract addresses OZ storage.rs:830: here spending_limit sorts first.

State for this rule lives in the account: the grant's rules, its record and the spending record. One authorization makes one contract call out of the account, to the verifier.

Step by step

Run the steps in order: each sees the ledger the previous steps left. A refused request is shown as the host's enforcing simulation of the signed transaction, which runs every __check_auth and policy exactly as applying it would; it is not submitted, and the page checks that the ledger fingerprint did not change. An allowed request is submitted and applied.

0Set up both ledgers

Reference run: reference: both set up

Each design gets its own local ledger: protocol-29 network settings, a funded fee payer, and nothing else. Setup uploads and deploys the contracts with ordinary signed transactions; a few balances and fixed contract addresses are placed directly, and are listed as simulator overrides.

OZ

Contracts: OpenZeppelin's v0.8.0 multisig account (8286422f…), the policy interpreter (6704996f…, deployed with the testnet pin's limits) and OpenZeppelin's v0.8.0 spending_limit (65e70aad…). The constructor makes rule 0: scope Default, signer Delegated(owner), no policy OZ account/contract.rs:32-41. The owner and the app are classic G accounts, so the host checks their signatures itself.

Not run yet.

Perch

Contracts: the Perch account (cc56a2d3…), its document compiler and its Ed25519 verifier, built from 0b3752d; these are the bytes the Perch paper embeds. The constructor installs the admin rule with the owner as an External Ed25519 signer Perch perch-account/lib.rs:34-36. The compiler and the verifier sit at the addresses the account derives from its build pins (an override), as in the paper's §10.

Not run yet.

1The owner installs the permission

Reference run: OZ: applied Perch: applied

The owner authorizes one administrative call on each account. On the OZ side it is add_context_rule with the arguments policy-synth built; on the Perch side, apply_grant(1, document).

OZ

The owner authorizes through rule 0, which has no policy, so OpenZeppelin requires every one of its signers in the payload OZ storage.rs:358-363, and the owner's own entry authorizes __check_auth with the preimage OZ storage.rs:396-413. add_context_rule stores rule 1 and installs its policies in address order OZ storage.rs:830 OZ storage.rs:803-870: spending_limit stores the window OZ spending_limit.rs:393-430; the interpreter checks the grammar version, the predicate's size and hash, that no signer or admin is External (#212), that the scope is not Default, the account or itself (#218), that the predicate reads the call, and the install nonce, then stores the predicate with a hash of the rule's signers OPB policy-interpreter/lib.rs:52-167.

Not run yet.

Perch

The owner's External key signs. rule_eval allows the call under the admin rule, then the verifier checks the owner's signature Perch gate.rs:71-151. apply_grant calls the stateless document compiler (canonical bytes, hash, model; the verifier canonicalizes the app's key), refuses a grant that escalates or is not in normal form, lowers it with rule-core's lower_scoped under the account, its excluded set and the grant generation, and stores grant 1 Perch perch-smart-account/lib.rs:1275-1383.

Not run yet.

2The app pays the shop 6 XLM

Reference run: OZ: applied Perch: applied

The request both rules exist for. Compare what each account needs signed.

OZ

Two entries. The account's entry carries no signature of its own: its AuthPayload names rule 1 and Delegated(app) with empty bytes. The app's own entry authorizes account.__check_auth(AuthDigestPreimage {account, [1], signature_payload}) and is signed with the app key OZ storage.rs:96-110 OZ storage.rs:396-413 OZ storage.rs:157-164. OpenZeppelin selects rule 1 for the transfer, finds the app on it, has the host check the app's entry, then runs the policies: spending_limit (0 + 6 ≤ 10; it records 6 at this ledger) and the interpreter (all five conjuncts hold) OZ storage.rs:629-689.

Not run yet.

Perch

One entry. Its AuthPayload names rule 1 and External(verifier, app key) with an Ed25519 signature over sha256(sha256("perch/account/auth-addr-v1" ‖ account ‖ payload) ‖ XDR([1])) Perch perch-smart-account/lib.rs:397-406 Perch gate.rs:134-138. rule_eval accepts: target, function, arguments 0 and 1, the signer condition, and 0 + 6 ≤ 10. The verifier then checks the signature, and the account stores the new spending record Perch gate.rs:71-151.

Not run yet.

3The app pays the shop 5 XLM more in the same window

Reference run: OZ: refused, #3221 Perch: refused, #5

Same signer and recipient as step 2; only the amount and the window's history differ.

OZ

Authentication passes. spending_limit evicts only spends at ledgers ≤ L − 100 OZ spending_limit.rs:486-505, so the 6 XLM stays, and 6 + 5 > 10 refuses with SpendingLimitExceeded (#3221) OZ spending_limit.rs:275-287. The interpreter never runs: spending_limit comes first in rule 1's policy list.

Not run yet.

Perch

rule_eval's cap check refuses, 6 + 5 > 10 rule-core cap.rs:169-205. The account reports every evaluator refusal except a stale grant as RuleEvalRefused, auth error 5 Perch gate.rs:121-133, so the code itself does not say which condition failed; this request differs from step 2 only in its amount. No verifier is called: Perch decides before it authenticates.

Not run yet.

4The app pays 1 XLM to Mallory

Reference run: OZ: refused, #100 Perch: refused, #5

A recipient the rule does not allow, well within the window.

OZ

Authentication passes. spending_limit, which does not look at the recipient, accepts and records 1 XLM; then the interpreter's call_arg 1 = shop fails with ArgMismatch (#100) OPB policy-interpreter/lib.rs:274-275 OPB storage.rs:51. The whole __check_auth fails, so the spending record's write is rolled back: the ledger fingerprint does not change.

Not run yet.

Perch

The rule's address-eq condition on argument 1 fails in rule_eval rule-core rule.rs:147-160 rule-core authorize.rs:105-132, refused as auth error 5; no verifier call.

Not run yet.

5Another key signs in the app's name

Reference run: OZ: refused, ed25519 check Perch: refused, ed25519 check

The request names the app as its signer, but the signature was made with a different key.

OZ

The account's entry still names Delegated(app); the app's entry carries the app's public key with another key's signature. When OpenZeppelin authenticates the app OZ storage.rs:396-413, the host checks that signature against the app's G account and fails ("failed ED25519 verification") host account_contract.rs:175-263 host crypto/mod.rs:78-93. No policy runs.

Not run yet.

Perch

The payload names External(verifier, app key) with another key's signature. rule_eval accepts, because the evaluator takes the claimed signers as given and the shell authenticates them afterwards Perch gate.rs:139-141. The verifier's Ed25519 check then traps with Error(Crypto, InvalidInput) Perch perch-ed25519-verifier/lib.rs:19-29 host crypto/mod.rs:78-93, so the authorization fails and nothing is stored. The account's own ExternalVerificationFailed (3003) Perch auth.rs:47-61 is not reached, because this verifier traps instead of returning false.

Not run yet.

6A key the rule does not list signs as itself

Reference run: OZ: refused, #3016 Perch: refused, #5

A valid signature, from a key that is not on the rule.

OZ

The payload names Delegated(stranger), which is on no selected rule: UnauthorizedSigner (#3016), before any signature is checked or any policy runs OZ storage.rs:667-674.

Not run yet.

Perch

rule_eval refuses: rule 1 requires the app, and the stranger is a signer of no chosen rule rule-core authorize.rs:105-132 rule-core authorize.rs:154-163. Auth error 5; no verifier call.

Not run yet.

7100 ledgers later, the app pays the shop 5 XLM

Reference run: OZ: applied Perch: applied

Close 100 ledgers, then repeat step 3's request.

OZ

spending_limit evicts spends at ledgers ≤ L − 100 OZ spending_limit.rs:486-505, so step 2's 6 XLM has left the window: 0 + 5 ≤ 10.

Not run yet.

Perch

rule-core's window holds the charges made after L − 100 and through L rule-core cap.rs:169-205; step 2's charge has left it: 0 + 5 ≤ 10. Both designs count the same window.

Not run yet.

Send your own request

After step 1 you can send other payments to the same two accounts, or close ledgers. Each request goes to both accounts unless you pick one.

Instruction counts come from this simulator's recording-mode host (soroban-env-host 29.0.2) under enforcing authorization, not stellar-core's exact metering, and measure two different contract stacks; they are not a performance result.

Findings to keep in mind

Observed in this page's run

  • OpenZeppelin runs a rule's policies in the order of their contract addresses OZ storage.rs:830. Here spending_limit runs first, so in step 4 it records the spend before the interpreter refuses the recipient; the refusal rolls that write back.
  • Perch's Ed25519 verifier traps on a bad signature instead of returning false Perch perch-ed25519-verifier/lib.rs:19-29, so in step 5 the wallet sees Error(Crypto, InvalidInput), not the account's ExternalVerificationFailed (3003) Perch auth.rs:47-61.
  • Perch reports every evaluator refusal except a stale grant as auth error 5 Perch gate.rs:121-133, so steps 3, 4 and 6 carry the same code; OpenZeppelin's codes name the component that refused.

What runs here, and what does not

  • Executed. The contracts' WebAssembly, rebuilt from source and byte-identical to the deployed or published bytes listed below; the Soroban host's authorization (tree matching, nonces, expiry, classic account signatures, __check_auth); soroban-sim's transaction validation and application for every allowed request. One Rust driver issues the same JSON commands natively and as this page's WebAssembly reactor; the native and in-browser runs agree on every returned field but wall-clock time.
  • Simulator substitutions. Each account has its own local ledger, forked from protocol-29 network settings recorded from testnet ledger 5,301,502, with the standalone passphrase Standalone Network ; February 2017. A throwaway fee payer is funded in the fork; the owner, app, stranger, shop and Mallory accounts are funded by override; Perch's compiler and verifier are placed at the addresses its build pins derive, as in the Perch paper's §10. Keys are throwaway software Ed25519 keys. One transaction closes one ledger.
  • Refusals are enforcing simulations. A refused request is not submitted, so this page makes no claim about the fee a failed, submitted transaction would pay.
  • Not shown (proposed for a later version). Passkey (WebAuthn) signers, OpenZeppelin threshold policies, External signers on the OZ side (the interpreter refuses them, #212 OPB policy-interpreter/lib.rs:458-465), rule expiry, signer rotation, revocation, Perch recovery and grant generations, and contract upgrades. The Perch paper's §10 covers recovery.
